approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a greedy population of molecules using score-weighted breeding, connected-fragment crossover and ordinary atom/bond mutations, with direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange disabled. Each suggestion generates a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process learns from the full chronological archive of accepted task-local scores, using folded radius-two chirality-aware Morgan occurrence counts and dot-product count Tanimoto covariance. It normalizes scores with their current mean and population standard deviation, keeps fixed observation noise, and selects new offspring by correlated sampled functions with sequential duplicate masks. Actual accepted scores immediately update the archive and greedy survivors.
approach.novelty: Apply one fixed exponential covariance warp to the existing count similarity: exp(T−1). This retains occurrence information, molecular features and similarity order while adding a common covariance floor and changing conditional regression and sampled-function correlation. Earlier siblings removed multiplicity, unfolded coordinates, added an atom-pair channel, replaced the learner with trees, or projected sampled residuals; this warp changes none of those interfaces. The separate same-round alternatives change the overlap formula or distance geometry. The test asks whether this particular covariance law improves ranking of real evaluated offspring and useful exploration, then meets the complete endpoint criterion.

hypothesis: Replace the original dot-product count Tanimoto covariance TDP by the fixed exponential warp K(x,y)=exp(TDP(x,y)-1), lambda=1, on the unchanged folded Morgan integer occurrence vectors, preserving the inherited TDP zero conventions and exact TDP=1 aliases.

finding_summary.headline: Exponential covariance changes allocation but loses 0.03228 despite more local wins
finding_summary.insights: The fixed law clearly executed; missing exposure, broken Gaussian arithmetic, passive fit failure or altered random draws do not explain the endpoint loss. Better prediction on the actively selected stream and more wins against weaker parents did not translate into higher absolute search quality. Productive new typed cores rose only from 280 to 288 and generic cores from 190 to 191; more later breeding also failed to recover the lost endpoints. All 150 terminal offspring in each panel remain censored, and 73 Child versus 50 Parent offspring had later breeding support but were never drawn. The molecular assessment associates the lower results with extended and geometrically uncertain families alongside conventional high-scoring alternatives; fewer unusual local bonds do not establish chemical stability or explain covariance contribution. The experiment narrows the case against this exact lambda-one warp under the tested composition and budget. It cannot tell us whether covariance-floor smoothing, omitted candidate rewards or subsequent feedback caused the loss, and selected-stream diagnostics do not establish pool-wide ranking or calibration. The registered complete gain test ends this exact law; a materially different future law needs a sourced distinguishing experiment.

These averages retain the losses: pair ordering worsened on every deco-hop seed and on one sitagliptin seed. Strict best-parent wins increased from 629 to 697 of 4350 offspring, and sequential incumbent advances from 258 to 273, but mean best-generating-parent score fell from 0.47046 to 0.44229; mean offspring score also fell slightly, from 0.38526 to 0.38235. Paired seed changes were −0.06839278, +0.00744768, −0.03588798; Child population SD was 0.00472367 versus 0.02659287. Median-2 improved in every seed, while deco-hop and docking lost in every seed. There were six task/seed wins and nine losses.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families and cyclic amines emerge, with reactive local bonds, uncertain polycycle geometry and unassigned stereo
molecular.overall_character: All 15 Child and all 15 published code-Parent trajectory paths and corresponding logs were present and read through the immutable request/evidence-index scope. No task is missing: each task has 900 accepted trajectory records, including 870 optimizer proposals; each cell has 300 records. Fake smoke is outside these trusted inputs. Accepted-record labels join all observations without mismatch. The Child chemistry spans aromatic carboxamides, extended azaaryl assemblies, ring/flexible amines, nitrogen-carbonyl polycycles and fluorinated imino/dione systems. Rings and aromaticity are rich, consistent with optimizer ring-text incidences 0.9954 to 1.0 and aromatic-text incidences 0.9862 to 1.0. Many framework types are explored, but seed-local leaders repeatedly refine limited families. Overall diversity is moderate; synthetic plausibility questionable and drug-likeness weak because familiar functionality is repeatedly combined with reactive bond environments, high mass in extended families and geometrically uncertain rings. No atom inheritance, synthesis, stability, protonation, conformation or biological activity was measured. The digest final excerpt only contains late seed-2 proposals, so complete trajectory maxima were used for seed endpoints. method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

finding_summary.insights: The fixed law clearly executed; missing exposure, broken Gaussian arithmetic, passive fit failure or altered random draws do not explain the endpoint loss. Better prediction on the actively selected stream and more wins against weaker parents did not translate into higher absolute search quality. Productive new typed cores rose only from 280 to 288 and generic cores from 190 to 191; more later breeding also failed to recover the lost endpoints. All 150 terminal offspring in each panel remain censored, and 73 Child versus 50 Parent offspring had later breeding support but were never drawn. The molecular assessment associates the lower results with extended and geometrically uncertain families alongside conventional high-scoring alternatives; fewer unusual local bonds do not establish chemical stability or explain covariance contribution. The experiment narrows the case against this exact lambda-one warp under the tested composition and budget. It cannot tell us whether covariance-floor smoothing, omitted candidate rewards or subsequent feedback caused the loss, and selected-stream diagnostics do not establish pool-wide ranking or calibration. The registered complete gain test ends this exact law; a materially different future law needs a sourced distinguishing experiment.

Paired seed changes were −0.06839278, +0.00744768, −0.03588798; Child population SD was 0.00472367 versus 0.02659287. Median-2 improved in every seed, while deco-hop and docking lost in every seed. There were six task/seed wins and nine losses.

Better prediction on the actively selected stream and more wins against weaker parents did not translate into higher absolute search quality. Productive new typed cores rose only from 280 to 288 and generic cores from 190 to 191; more later breeding also failed to recover the lost endpoints. All 150 terminal offspring in each panel remain censored, and 73 Child versus 50 Parent offspring had later breeding support but were never drawn. The molecular assessment associates the lower results with extended and geometrically uncertain families alongside conventional high-scoring alternatives; fewer unusual local bonds do not establish chemical stability or explain covariance contribution. The experiment narrows the case against this exact lambda-one warp under the tested composition and budget. It cannot tell us whether covariance-floor smoothing, omitted candidate rewards or subsequent feedback caused the loss, and selected-stream diagnostics do not establish pool-wide ranking or calibration. The registered complete gain test ends this exact law; a materially different future law needs a sourced distinguishing experiment.
finding_summary.results: All 15 task/seed evaluations completed. Selected sets changed in 417 of 435 batches, with 1230 active selections outside the passive original set. On the actual Child emissions, MSE fell from 0.007744 with passive original predictions to 0.007064, pair-order accuracy rose from 66.48% to 67.19%, and mean within-batch Spearman rose from 0.4279 to 0.4417. These averages retain the losses: pair ordering worsened on every deco-hop seed and on one sitagliptin seed. Strict best-parent wins increased from 629 to 697 of 4350 offspring, and sequential incumbent advances from 258 to 273, but mean best-generating-parent score fell from 0.47046 to 0.44229; mean offspring score also fell slightly, from 0.38526 to 0.38235. Total incumbent gain fell from 5.80766 to 5.32350. Final macro score decreased from 0.59566965 to 0.56339196, a mean loss of 0.03227769 against the required gain of 0.002. Paired seed changes were −0.06839278, +0.00744768, −0.03588798; Child population SD was 0.00472367 versus 0.02659287. Median-2 improved in every seed, while deco-hop and docking lost in every seed. There were six task/seed wins and nine losses.

The Child chemistry spans aromatic carboxamides, extended azaaryl assemblies, ring/flexible amines, nitrogen-carbonyl polycycles and fluorinated imino/dione systems. Many framework types are explored, but seed-local leaders repeatedly refine limited families. Overall diversity is moderate; synthetic plausibility questionable and drug-likeness weak because familiar functionality is repeatedly combined with reactive bond environments, high mass in extended families and geometrically uncertain rings.
